substantive_tests.name: unfamiliar capacity reservation

given_inputs.decision: Read both rows; increase only own row if total plus six is at most ten.
given_inputs.assumptions: Separate full transactions; ordinary reads; no extra constraint or coordinating lock.

substantive_tests.conclusion: Overlapping old views permit twelve reserved units, exceeding capacity. Either serial order reserves only six. Serializable must prevent both successful conflicting decisions.

substantive_tests.name: relative UPDATE versus stale replacement
substantive_tests.given_inputs: PostgreSQL Read Committed; one row n=100; two separate full transactions; both commit; no trigger or other writer.
substantive_tests.relative_update: Both run UPDATE SET n=n+1; a waiting writer applies to the newer row, so final n=102.
substantive_tests.stale_replacement: Both first SELECT 100 and later issue UPDATE SET n=101; row locking orders the writes but both chosen constants are 101, so final n=101.
substantive_tests.conclusion: Concurrent does not automatically mean incorrect; SQL expression and transaction decision matter.

substantive_tests.name: serializable cannot repair split operation boundaries
substantive_tests.given_inputs: Capacity ten; two callers each read zero in its own committed transaction, then each updates its own reservation row to six in a separate serializable transaction.
substantive_tests.result: Total twelve; SQL transactions are serially ordered but the complete application decision was split.
substantive_tests.conclusion: Serializable composition requires each whole decision to be in its transaction.
